title: Comprehensive Buying Guide for 75mm Threaded Pipe: Selection Tips and Pricing
html:
Introduction: Why the 75 mm threaded pipe matters in modern irrigation?

In pressurized irrigation systems, particularly drip line and drip irrigation methods, the choice of main pipe plays a vital role in the overall system performance. Due to their appropriate flow capacity, 75 mm diameter pipes are among the most commonly used sizes in medium and large farms. These pipes are typically supplied as threaded pipes , which makes installation faster and safer than welding or copper crimping methods. A correct understanding of technical characteristics, manufacturing standards, and price-influencing factors helps farmers make better investments and prevent resource waste.

In this article from the Irrigation Line website, we examine all technical and economic aspects of purchasing this type of pipe. Our goal is to expose you to common challenges and, by providing practical solutions, assist in making clear and informed decisions. Please stay with us to learn important details such as material composition, UV resistance, and connection methods.

Technical features of 75 mm threaded pipe

To select a high-quality pipe, you must have a precise understanding of its technical parameters. 75-millimeter pipes are typically made from high-density polyethylene (HDPE) or UHMW-PE. Due to their flexibility, chemical resistance, and corrosion-free nature, these materials are the preferred option for agricultural irrigation.

Material and wall thickness

  • Polymer density: Pipes with better granulation generally contain a higher percentage of pure base material. This directly affects the service life of the pipe.
  • Thickness (SDR): The greater the wall thickness, the higher the internal pressure tolerance. For drip line irrigation with standard operating pressure, selecting the appropriate SDR prevents pipe bursting.
  • UV resistance: In hot regions with intense sunlight, selecting pipes containing anti-UV additives prevents cracking of the outer surface. To learn more about this topic, you can read the article on important tips for using water drip lines.

Connection method and threading standard

The "threaded" section refers to the presence of external or helical threads at the end of the pipe, which allows for the quick connection of fittings, valves, and side components. Precision in thread pitch and thread depth is critical. A high-quality pipe features clean threads, free from burrs, with precise angles for a secure fit with standard connections. This feature reduces leakage at connection points, a primary cause of pressure loss in drip irrigation systems.

Buying guide and price review for 75 mm threaded pipe

The price of irrigation pipes varies and depends on multiple factors. As a buying guide, one should not focus solely on the lowest price, as low quality leads to premature wear and higher replacement costs. Below, we examine the key factors that determine price and ensure the correct purchase.

Factors affecting the final price

  1. Raw material fluctuations: Global oil and petrochemical prices directly impact polymer production costs.
  2. Brand and Manufacturer: Domestically produced items with high quality usually have more competitive prices than imported ones, but you must verify the authenticity of the product.
  3. Transportation Cost: Considering the weight of 75 mm pipes, the distance from the production center can affect the total cost.

When requesting a quote, always ask the seller to specify the exact material grade (such as PE80 or PE100) and wall thickness. To better understand overhead costs in irrigation systems, reading the article "How much does it cost to equip one hectare with drip tape?" can give you a broader perspective.

Key Points During Quotation and Purchase

  • Always request physical samples or clear images of the threads and pipe cross-section.
  • Ensure written warranty or returnability in case of structural defects.
  • Compare prices on a 'price per meter' basis, not just the price per reel.

Applications and practical installation tips

75 mm polyethylene pipe is typically used as the main line in larger systems or as a sub-line in smaller systems. In drip irrigation, this pipe functions as the main loop, to which driplines are connected. Here are several practical tips for optimal installation:

Pressure distribution and hydraulic calculations

Before purchasing, hydraulic calculations must be performed to ensure that the 75 mm pipe does not experience unacceptable pressure loss under your specific field conditions (line length, elevation difference, and discharge flow rate). If your system is complex, you may need pipes of different sizes, such as 3-inch polyethylene pipe or others, which should be selected based on engineering calculations.

Planting at appropriate depth

To extend the pipe's lifespan, it is recommended to plant the 75 mm main pipe at a reduced depth (Shadow Zone). This prevents physical damage from machinery and UV radiation. Additionally, when designing the network, you should consider modern farmland irrigation methods to ensure pipe size selection aligns with the optimal irrigation method.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Is a 75 mm pipe sufficient for small farms?

Depending on the total system flow rate and line length, 75 mm may be too large or too small. If the total flow is under one cubic meter per hour, smaller sizes like 50 or 63 mm may be more efficient. However, for most industrial drip systems, 75 mm provides a good balance between cost and performance.

What is the difference between a 75 mm pipe and a 3-inch pipe?

A 3-inch pipe is equivalent to an internal diameter of approximately 76–80 mm. In European and Iranian standards, we use the metric system (OD). A "75 mm" pipe refers to the Outer Diameter (OD), while a 3-inch pipe follows the Nominal Diameter. When purchasing, always specify whether you require 75mm OD or Inches.

Do threaded fittings require gaskets?

Yes, standard loose fittings and screw connections usually require metal or rubber gaskets to ensure leak prevention at the thread points. The use of Teflon tape may also be helpful for small threaded connections.

Summary

Purchasing a 75 mm threaded pipe is a techno-economic decision that directly impacts your irrigation efficiency and crop yield. By selecting the appropriate material, paying close attention to wall thickness, and following installation guidelines, you can establish a durable and cost-effective system. Always request quotes from reputable suppliers and verify the quality of the threads. For more details on other system components, we recommend reading our article on yield per hectare to better understand the relationship between irrigation infrastructure and final production.

We hope this guide has been helpful in selecting the right irrigation pipes for your needs. If you have any technical questions, you can contact our specialized team.
